14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```
335: 
336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
340: 
341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
350: \```[language]
351: // Bad code with issues
352: // Showing what NOT to do
353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
356: \```[language]
357: // Good code with fixes
358: // Showing correct approach
359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale
369: 
370: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:
375: ```markdown
376: ### Common Patterns
377: 
378: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
379: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
380: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
385: 
386: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
387: 
388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
389: 
390: **Format**:
391: \```markdown
392: ### Decision Logic
393: 
394: \```markdown
395: IF [condition A]:
396:   → [Action/Path A]
397:   → [Expected outcome A]
398: 
399: IF [condition B]:
400:   → [Action/Path B]
401:   → [Expected outcome B]
402: 
403: IF [condition C]:
404:   → [Action/Path C]
405:   → [Expected outcome C]
406: \```
407: \```
408: 
409: **Alternative format** (decision tree):
410: \```markdown
411: \```
412: Analyze situation
413: ├─ Condition A met
414: │  └─ Execute Workflow A
415: │     └─ Expected outcome A
416: ├─ Condition B met
417: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
418: │     └─ Expected outcome B
419: └─ Condition C met
420:    └─ Execute Workflow C
421:       └─ Expected outcome C
422: \```
423: \```
424: 
425: ### Validation Checkpoints
426: 
427: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows
428: 
429: **Format**:
430: ```markdown
431: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
432: ```
433: 
434: **Examples**:
435: - `files_analyzed`
436: - `artifacts_filtered`
437: - `strategy_determined`
438: - `root_cause_identified`
439: 
440: **Usage**: Reference in quality checklists and debugging
441: 
442: ### Prerequisites Section
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Link to required standards and context
445: 
446: > **PLACEMENT**: Prerequisites go in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph.
447: 
448: **Format**:
449: ```markdown
450: # [Workflow Name]
451: 
452: [1-2 sentence summary only - no prerequisites here]
453:

455:

457:

459: Follow [standard name] for all implementations:
460: - **[Standard 1]**: [Brief description]

462: - See [standard-file.md](./standard-file.md) for complete requirements
463: ```
464: 
465: **Key Elements**:
466: - Appears in Section 1 OVERVIEW, not intro
467: - Links to other reference files

472: **Purpose**: Show MCP tool usage, script execution, asset references
473: 
474: **Format for MCP Tools**:

477:

490: **What you'll see:**

501: \```

513: ### Common Error Patterns
514: 
515: **Purpose**: Document actual errors with explanations
516: 
517: **Format**:
518: \```markdown
519: **Common [System/Browser] Errors:**
520: 
521: \```javascript
522: // [Actual error message]
523: // → [What it means]
524: // → [How to fix]
525: 
526: // [Another error message]
527: // → [What it means]
528: // → [How to fix]
529: \```
530: \```
531: 
532: **Example**:
533: \```markdown
534: **Common Browser Errors:**
535: 
536: \```javascript
537: // Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'X' of undefined
538: // → Variable is undefined, check initialization
539: // → Verify element exists before accessing properties
540: 
541: // Failed to load resource: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT
542: // → Ad blocker or browser extension blocking resource
543: // → Check Network tab, test with extensions disabled
544: \```
545: \```

548: 
549: **Purpose**: Explicitly state what's in/out of scope
550: 
551: **Format**:

554: 
555: **Out of scope:** [What is NOT supported]
556: ```

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```

120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |

135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.

138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166:

192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)

252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead

346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006:

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

15: # Manual Testing Playbook Conversation Scenarios
16: 
17: This reference defines the closed script format for conversation scenarios in a manual testing playbook. The validator checks the script, and the runner executes the same parsed script.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: Write a conversation scenario when the behavior depends on multiple prompts, scripted answers, runtime actions, or state checks across a session. One prompt is enough when a single request and its result capture the full behavior. The ordered decision rule, the runtime requirements and the cost of each style live in `SKILL.md` §6, Choosing the Scenario Style.
24: 
25: The script is one fenced `json conversation` block in section 3 of the scenario file. The block is the source of truth for the conversation turns.
26: 
27: ---
28: 
29: ## 2. ROLES
30: 
31: - **Orchestrator**: The runner or an operator who runs the script by hand. It plays the human by pausing, typing each turn, answering expected questions, and running the state check.
32: - **Subject**: The runtime's interactive session under test, started in a scratch project. It never sees the script, only what the orchestrator types.
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 3. BLOCK SCHEMA
37: 
38: The validator accepts only the keys in this table. Any other key is an error, so a misspelled key cannot fall back to a default.
39: 
40: | Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
41: |-----|------|----------|---------|
42: | `runtimes` | array of strings | Yes | The runtimes this script is written for, from `claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex`, `pi` and `devin` |
43: | `setup` | array of strings | No | Runs before the subject starts. Exit 77 skips the runtime with the first non-empty output line as the blocker. Other nonzero exits refuse the run as `SETUP_FAILED` |
44: | `env` | object of strings | No | Variables added to the subject's environment, such as a kill switch |
45: | `trust_hooks` | boolean | No | When true, the runner trusts the project's hooks on a runtime that asks, which is Codex today, so they fire during the run. The runner records each trust entry for the run's scratch project that the subject adds to or changes in the operator's Codex config, removes or restores it after the run, and writes the result to `hook-trust.json`. Entries for other folders, which another Codex session may be writing, are listed under `outside_project` and left alone. Codex's review screen also lists the user's own changed global hooks, so the runner picks "Trust all" only when the screen's count of new or changed hooks is no larger than the handlers in the project's `.codex/hooks.json`; otherwise it continues without trusting and fails the run with `HOOK_TRUST_OUTSIDE_PROJECT`. Defaults to false, which leaves hooks untrusted |
46: | `turns` | array of turn objects | Yes | The conversation, in order. The first turn holding `send` or `action` must be a `send` |
47: | `turns[].id` | string | No | Name used for the turn's evidence folder. Defaults to the 1-based position. Unique |
48: | `turns[].send` | string | At most one of `send` or `action` | What the human types, on one line. A turn with neither is a check-only turn, such as a baseline before the first send |
49: | `turns[].action` | `restart` or `compact` | At most one of `send` or `action` | Restart the subject into the same session, or compact its context. Compaction followed by a send is two turns |
50: | `turns[].delay_ms` | integer 0 or more, or `[min, max]` | No | The human's pause before the turn starts. A pair draws from a generator seeded by the runner's `--seed`. Defaults to 2000 |
51: | `turns[].timeout_ms` | integer, 1 or more | No | The longest the turn may run before it fails. Defaults to 300000 |
52: | `turns[].retry` | 0 or 1 | No | Run a failed turn once more before the failure ends the run. Defaults to 0 |
53: | `turns[].questions` | array | No | The questions the subject should ask during this turn, each with its scripted answer |
54: | `turns[].questions[].match` | string | Yes | A regular expression tested against the question text. A question that wraps onto several screen lines is joined into one line first |
55: | `turns[].questions[].answer` | object | Yes | Exactly one of `select`, `other` or `reply` |
56: | `answer.select` | array of strings, not empty | | Option labels to choose in a question-tool dialog. Two or more labels need `multi: true`. A label matches an option exactly, ignoring case, or else the one option that contains it, so `Skip` chooses `D) Skip documentation (Recommended)`. A label that fits several options fails the turn |
57: | `answer.multi` | boolean | No | Marks a multi-select. Only valid beside `select`. Defaults to false |
58: | `answer.other` | string | | Text typed into the dialog's free-text row |
59: | `answer.reply` | string | | A plain chat message, for a question the subject asked in chat |
60: | `turns[].questions[].delay_ms` | integer 0 or more, or `[min, max]` | No | The human's pause after the question renders and before answering. Defaults to 1000 |
61: | `turns[].questions[].optional` | boolean | No | When true, the turn still passes if the subject never asks. Defaults to false |
62: | `turns[].check` | string | Yes | A shell command run in the scratch project after the turn settles |
63: 
64: The validator parses the block but never runs `setup` or `check` commands.
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 4. TURN OUTCOMES
69: 
70: - A setup command that exits 77 skips the runtime and records its first non-empty output line as the blocker. The subject is not launched. Other nonzero exits refuse the run as `SETUP_FAILED`.
71: - A question that matches no entry fails the turn. A required question entry that the subject never asks also fails the turn. An entry with `optional: true` does not fail the turn when the subject never asks.
72: - A check that exits 0 passes the turn. Exit 77 skips that turn, records `SKIP` and uses the first non-empty output line as its blocker. Any other exit fails the turn.
73: - The last non-empty output line from the check is the observed value.
74: - A failed turn with `retry: 1` runs once more. Both attempts are recorded. After a failure ends the runtime's run, later turns are recorded as `NOT_RUN`.
75: - A skipped turn does not end the runtime's run.
76: - A check-only turn has neither `send` nor `action`. The first turn with either field must use `send`.
77: - When a launch or a turn has already failed, the runner reads the screen once, and a line that matches a usage-limit message names the failure `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` and becomes its blocker. A passing turn is never reclassified, and only Codex's wording (`You've hit your usage limit`) is confirmed from a recorded screen, while the other runtimes' patterns are their known wording, not yet seen live.
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 5. EVIDENCE EACH TURN LEAVES
82: 
83: Each turn leaves the following evidence:
84: 
85: - The screen after the turn settles.
86: - The screen at each question.
87: - The check's output and exit code.
88: - The turn's slice of raw pane output in `raw-pane.log`.
89: - The pane's full plain-text scrollback in `history.txt`.
90: - One line per keystroke group in the run's action log.
91: - The turn's start and end times.
92: - One `checkpoints.tsv` row per turn with the turn id, status, attempts, evidence folder, and observed value.
93: 
94: The raw pane slice and `history.txt` exist when the check runs, so a check can read both from `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. `history.txt` holds the full plain-text scrollback and is the right file to search for text that a long reply may have scrolled off the 50-row `screen.txt`. `raw-pane.log` carries terminal escape codes between words, so a plain `grep` on it is unreliable.
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 6. COMPLETE EXAMPLE
99: 
100: ```json conversation
101: {
102:   "runtimes": ["claude-code", "opencode", "pi", "devin"],
103:   "turns": [
104:     {
105:       "id": "pick-color",
106:       "send": "Ask me which color to use with your question tool, offering red, green and blue, then write my answer to answers.txt.",
107:       "delay_ms": 3000,
108:       "questions": [{ "match": "colou?r", "answer": { "select": ["green"] } }],
109:       "check": "grep -qx green answers.txt"
110:     },
111:     { "id": "resume", "action": "restart", "check": "test -s answers.txt" }
112:   ]
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## 7. AUTHORING RULES
119: 
120: - Start the scenario file from `assets/manual-testing-playbook-conversation-snippet-template.md`.
121: - Put one `json conversation` block in each scenario file under `### Conversation Script` in section 3.
122: - The first `send` must equal the scenario contract prompt.
123: - A second scratch project or a different `env` is a separate scenario file and runner invocation.
124: - Compaction followed by a send is two turns: one turn with `action: compact` and its check, then a turn with the send.
125: - A turn with neither `send` nor `action` is check-only. The first turn holding one of those fields must be a `send`.
126: - The validator checks the block but never runs `setup` or `check` commands.
127: - Never match a model reply with `grep -x` or `grep -Fx` on `screen.txt`. Runtime prefixes prevent an exact line match: Claude replies start with `⏺ `, Codex with `• `, Pi with ` ● `, Devin with a leading space and OpenCode with five spaces. Use `grep -F` with a distinctive marker.
128: - `screen.txt` shows a visible 50-row pane that retains earlier turns and the current turn's echoed send. Inspect only text after that turn's echoed send by using the `awk` pattern in [the session resume example](../../../../skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-claude-code/manual-testing-playbook/session-continuity/resume-specific-session-by-id-conversation.md), or check a marker the model can learn only by reading a file. Never put the expected marker in a `send`.
129: - A check can read the turn's evidence from `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. The raw pane slice in `raw-pane.log` and the full plain-text scrollback in `history.txt` both exist before the check runs. `history.txt` is the right file to search for text that a long reply may have scrolled off the 50-row `screen.txt`. `raw-pane.log` carries terminal escape codes between words, so a plain `grep` on it is unreliable.
130: - The scratch project inherits the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so before any file write the model asks the spec-folder question in plain chat. For every turn that writes, add a `questions` entry with `"answer": {"reply": "D"}` and `"optional": true`. An `other` answer belongs only in a runtime question dialog, never in plain chat. Use `reply` for chat questions.
131: - The scratch starts without skills. When a scenario needs a skill, setup must copy the repository skills and the runtime project configuration into scratch with `cp -R "$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT/.skilled" .skilled` and `cp -R "$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT/.claude" .claude`, replacing `.claude` with `.opencode`, `.pi` or `.devin` when that runtime requires it. Their relative symlinks resolve after `.skilled` is copied. Never symlink into the repository because the runner refuses the run with `CONTAINMENT_ESCAPED`.
132: - Do not coach the behavior under test. Each `send` must be the plain user request. Do not tell the model to ask a question, pause, refuse or name which tool it used.
133: - A question's `match` regular expression must identify the question asked and must not match any text in the echoed `send`.
134: - If a required precondition is missing, such as a fixture, credential, tool or network access, setup must exit with status `77` and print a one-line reason to skip the runtime. Its first non-empty output line is the blocker. A check can exit `77` to skip its turn.
135: - Checks must only read state. Nothing may write under `$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## 8. RUNNING A SCRIPT
140: 
141: Run the script from the repository root:
142: 
143: ```bash
144: node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/scripts/run-conversation-scenario.cjs --scenario <file.md> --runtime <id[,id...]> --scratch <scratch-dir> --out <evidence-dir> [--seed N] [--overwrite] [--no-sandbox]
145: ```
146: 
147: The runtime list accepts `claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex`, `pi` and `devin`. The scratch directory must be outside the repository. The evidence directory gets one subfolder per requested runtime.
148: 
149: Exit status `0` means every runtime passed or skipped. Exit status `1` means at least one runtime failed. Exit status `2` means a usage error or a refused run.
150: 
151: Each runtime folder contains `result.json`, `actions.jsonl`, `raw-pane.log`, `setup.log`, `repo-before.txt`, `repo-after.txt` and `checkpoints.tsv`. Each turn folder contains `screen.txt`, `history.txt`, its `raw-pane.log` slice, one `question-N.txt` file per detected question and `check.txt`. The evidence root contains `matrix.md`, with one verdict and evidence path per requested runtime.
152: 
153: The runner sets `CONVERSATION_RUNTIME`, `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT`, `CONVERSATION_RUN_DIR` (the runtime's evidence folder) and `CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR` (the turn's evidence folder) for each `check` command. A check defaults to 60 seconds. Set `CONVERSATION_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` to override that bound. An overrun fails as `CHECK_TIMEOUT`. Each `setup` command has 120 seconds. An overrun refuses the run as `SETUP_TIMEOUT`. Exit 77 skips the runtime with its first non-empty output line as the blocker. The runner sets `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT` and `CONVERSATION_RUNTIME` for every `setup` command too, so setup can copy project files from the repository without any variable set by hand. `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT` is the repository the run snapshots, which `--repo-root` can point at a worktree.
154: 
155: Use `--seed N` to replay random delays declared as `[min, max]`. The runner records the seed in `result.json`. Use `--overwrite` to replace existing per-runtime evidence folders. Without it, the runner refuses a non-empty runtime folder.
156: 
157: Before and after each runtime run, the runner hashes the repository's `specs/` folder and its watched `.skilled/skills/.state/` subfolders by path, size and SHA-256. The watched subfolder is `decision-capture` by default. Set `CONVERSATION_WATCH` to a comma-separated list of subfolder names to watch others. A difference fails that runtime as `REPO_CHANGED` and keeps both snapshots in its evidence folder.
158: 
159: On macOS the runner starts Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi and Devin through `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` with a profile that denies writes under the repository root, under the checkout the runner lives in and under the git common dir. Codex is not wrapped, because it keeps its own `--sandbox workspace-write` and one seatbelt profile cannot be applied inside another. `--no-sandbox` turns the wrapper off. Each runtime's `result.json` gains a `sandbox` key holding `seatbelt`, `codex-workspace-write`, `off` or `unavailable`. When `sandbox-exec` is missing or the host is not macOS, the value is `unavailable` and the runner writes one stderr line saying the subject runs unsandboxed. The snapshot check still runs either way.
160: 
161: ---
162: 
163: ## 9. PER-RUNTIME NOTES
164: 
165: | Runtime | Probe status | Recorded behavior |
166: |---------|--------------|-------------------|
167: | Claude Code | probed | Version 2.1.316. The `AskUserQuestion` dialog supports single-select, multi-select and a free-text Other row. The probe records arrow and Enter navigation, `/compact` and resume through the same session ID. |
168: | OpenCode | probed | Version 2.1.4. Session ids must start with `ses_`, so the runner derives one from its UUID and the same `--session` flag resumes it. The `question` dialog toggles a multi-select row with Enter and submits from its Submit tab; the free-text row opens with Enter. The model comes from the root `opencode.json`, which setup must copy. |
169: | Codex | probed | Version 0.164.0. Start-up can show a folder-trust screen, an update offer (always skipped) and a hook review. Hooks stay untrusted unless the script sets `trust_hooks`; then the runner picks "Trust all and continue" and undoes those trust entries after the run. `request_user_input` offers one choice per question, so several choices or an Other answer are typed as a note on its `None of the above` row. Restart uses `codex resume --last` in the scratch folder. Enter must wait 500 ms after typed text, or it lands inside the paste. |
170: | Pi | probed | Version 1.4.0. Two question tools: `question` draws a pick list ending in `Done (...)`, and `ask_user_question` draws a dialog with Space to toggle and a Submit row. The run quits with `/quit`, because `/exit` is sent to the model. `/compact` refuses a session that is still small. |
171: | Devin | probed | Version 3000.11.234. A folder-trust screen opens the first run. The dialog toggles a multi-select row with Space and confirms with Enter; the Other row takes typed text directly. Restart uses `devin --continue` in the scratch folder. Enter must wait 500 ms after typed text. |
172: 
173: Each live MTP-007 run must record the model used by every runtime beside `matrix.md`. If a runtime does not expose its model, record `UNKNOWN` and note what you checked.
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: ## 10. MULTI-RUNTIME LIVE TESTS
178: 
179: Use the script fields below to cover a multi-runtime live test:
180: 
181: | Need | Script form |
182: |------|-------------|
183: | Single-select, multi-select or Other tool question | Use `answer.select` with one or several labels, or `answer.other` for free text. Set `multi: true` when selecting several labels. |
184: | Question asked in plain chat | Use `answer.reply`. |
185: | Process question that must leave no trace | Add an expected question entry, usually `optional: true` when runtimes differ. The turn check asserts that the captured state has no trace. |
186: | Mid-run or final save | Use a `send` turn that requests the save, then a `check` that copies saved files into `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. |
187: | Restart or compaction | Use `action: "restart"` or `action: "compact"`, followed by a state check. |
188: | Kill switch | Put the switch in a separate scenario file's `env` and check that the run wrote nothing. |
189: | Named stages and per-turn state copies | Give each turn an `id` and use its `check` to copy state into `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. |
190: | Runtime results | Pass a comma-separated `--runtime` list. Review each row and evidence path in `matrix.md`. |
191: | Model used | Record each runtime's model next to `matrix.md`. The runner matrix does not have a model column. |
192: 
193: The scenario's `setup` must copy each available runtime project configuration from `$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT` into the scratch project: `.claude/`, `.opencode/`, the root `opencode.json`, `.codex/`, `.pi/` and `.devin/`. Skip a configuration directory when it is missing. The live test then exercises the same project instructions the runtime would read in the repository.
194: 
195: ---
196:
