77: - When a launch or a turn has already failed, the runner reads the screen once, and a line that matches a usage-limit message names the failure `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` and becomes its blocker. A passing turn is never reclassified, and only Codex's wording (`You've hit your usage limit`) is confirmed from a recorded screen, while the other runtimes' patterns are their known wording, not yet seen live.
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 5. EVIDENCE EACH TURN LEAVES
82: 
83: Each turn leaves the following evidence:
84: 
85: - The screen after the turn settles.
86: - The screen at each question.
87: - The check's output and exit code.
88: - The turn's slice of raw pane output in `raw-pane.log`.
89: - The pane's full plain-text scrollback in `history.txt`.
90: - One line per keystroke group in the run's action log.
91: - The turn's start and end times.
92: - One `checkpoints.tsv` row per turn with the turn id, status, attempts, evidence folder, and observed value.
93: 
94: The raw pane slice and `history.txt` exist when the check runs, so a check can read both from `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. `history.txt` holds the full plain-text scrollback and is the right file to search for text that a long reply may have scrolled off the 50-row `screen.txt`. `raw-pane.log` carries terminal escape codes between words, so a plain `grep` on it is unreliable.
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 6. COMPLETE EXAMPLE
99: 
100: ```json conversation
101: {
102:   "runtimes": ["claude-code", "opencode", "pi", "devin"],
103:   "turns": [
104:     {
105:       "id": "pick-color",
106:       "send": "Ask me which color to use with your question tool, offering red, green and blue, then write my answer to answers.txt.",
107:       "delay_ms": 3000,
108:       "questions": [{ "match": "colou?r", "answer": { "select": ["green"] } }],
109:       "check": "grep -qx green answers.txt"
110:     },
111:     { "id": "resume", "action": "restart", "check": "test -s answers.txt" }
112:   ]
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## 7. AUTHORING RULES
119: 
120: - Start the scenario file from `assets/manual-testing-playbook-conversation-snippet-template.md`.
121: - Put one `json conversation` block in each scenario file under `### Conversation Script` in section 3.
122: - The first `send` must equal the scenario contract prompt.
123: - A second scratch project or a different `env` is a separate scenario file and runner invocation.
124: - Compaction followed by a send is two turns: one turn with `action: compact` and its check, then a turn with the send.
125: - A turn with neither `send` nor `action` is check-only. The first turn holding one of those fields must be a `send`.
126: - The validator checks the block but never runs `setup` or `check` commands.
127: - Never match a model reply with `grep -x` or `grep -Fx` on `screen.txt`. Runtime prefixes prevent an exact line match: Claude replies start with `⏺ `, Codex with `• `, Pi with ` ● `, Devin with a leading space and OpenCode with five spaces. Use `grep -F` with a distinctive marker.
128: - `screen.txt` shows a visible 50-row pane that retains earlier turns and the current turn's echoed send. Inspect only text after that turn's echoed send by using the `awk` pattern in [the session resume example](../../../../skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-claude-code/manual-testing-playbook/session-continuity/resume-specific-session-by-id-conversation.md), or check a marker the model can learn only by reading a file. Never put the expected marker in a `send`.
129: - A check can read the turn's evidence from `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. The raw pane slice in `raw-pane.log` and the full plain-text scrollback in `history.txt` both exist before the check runs. `history.txt` is the right file to search for text that a long reply may have scrolled off the 50-row `screen.txt`. `raw-pane.log` carries terminal escape codes between words, so a plain `grep` on it is unreliable.
130: - The scratch project inherits the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so before any file write the model asks the spec-folder question in plain chat. For every turn that writes, add a `questions` entry with `"answer": {"reply": "D"}` and `"optional": true`. An `other` answer belongs only in a runtime question dialog, never in plain chat. Use `reply` for chat questions.
131: - The scratch starts without skills. When a scenario needs a skill, setup must copy the repository skills and the runtime project configuration into scratch with `cp -R "$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT/.skilled" .skilled` and `cp -R "$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT/.claude" .claude`, replacing `.claude` with `.opencode`, `.pi` or `.devin` when that runtime requires it. Their relative symlinks resolve after `.skilled` is copied. Never symlink into the repository because the runner refuses the run with `CONTAINMENT_ESCAPED`.
132: - Do not coach the behavior under test. Each `send` must be the plain user request. Do not tell the model to ask a question, pause, refuse or name which tool it used.
133: - A question's `match` regular expression must identify the question asked and must not match any text in the echoed `send`.
134: - If a required precondition is missing, such as a fixture, credential, tool or network access, setup must exit with status `77` and print a one-line reason to skip the runtime. Its first non-empty output line is the blocker. A check can exit `77` to skip its turn.
135: - Checks must only read state. Nothing may write under `$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## 8. RUNNING A SCRIPT
140: 
141: Run the script from the repository root:
142: 
143: ```bash
144: node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/scripts/run-conversation-scenario.cjs --scenario <file.md> --runtime <id[,id...]> --scratch <scratch-dir> --out <evidence-dir> [--seed N] [--overwrite] [--no-sandbox]
145: ```
146: 
147: The runtime list accepts `claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex`, `pi` and `devin`. The scratch directory must be outside the repository. The evidence directory gets one subfolder per requested runtime.
148: 
149: Exit status `0` means every runtime passed or skipped. Exit status `1` means at least one runtime failed. Exit status `2` means a usage error or a refused run.
150: 
151: Each runtime folder contains `result.json`, `actions.jsonl`, `raw-pane.log`, `setup.log`, `repo-before.txt`, `repo-after.txt` and `checkpoints.tsv`. Each turn folder contains `screen.txt`, `history.txt`, its `raw-pane.log` slice, one `question-N.txt` file per detected question and `check.txt`. The evidence root contains `matrix.md`, with one verdict and evidence path per requested runtime.
152: 
153: The runner sets `CONVERSATION_RUNTIME`, `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT`, `CONVERSATION_RUN_DIR` (the runtime's evidence folder) and `CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR` (the turn's evidence folder) for each `check` command. A check defaults to 60 seconds. Set `CONVERSATION_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` to override that bound. An overrun fails as `CHECK_TIMEOUT`. Each `setup` command has 120 seconds. An overrun refuses the run as `SETUP_TIMEOUT`. Exit 77 skips the runtime with its first non-empty output line as the blocker. The runner sets `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT` and `CONVERSATION_RUNTIME` for every `setup` command too, so setup can copy project files from the repository without any variable set by hand. `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT` is the repository the run snapshots, which `--repo-root` can point at a worktree.
154: 
155: Use `--seed N` to replay random delays declared as `[min, max]`. The runner records the seed in `result.json`. Use `--overwrite` to replace existing per-runtime evidence folders. Without it, the runner refuses a non-empty runtime folder.
156: 
157: Before and after each runtime run, the runner hashes the repository's `specs/` folder and its watched `.skilled/skills/.state/` subfolders by path, size and SHA-256. The watched subfolder is `decision-capture` by default. Set `CONVERSATION_WATCH` to a comma-separated list of subfolder names to watch others. A difference fails that runtime as `REPO_CHANGED` and keeps both snapshots in its evidence folder.
158: 
159: On macOS the runner starts Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi and Devin through `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` with a profile that denies writes under the repository root, under the checkout the runner lives in and under the git common dir. Codex is not wrapped, because it keeps its own `--sandbox workspace-write` and one seatbelt profile cannot be applied inside another. `--no-sandbox` turns the wrapper off. Each runtime's `result.json` gains a `sandbox` key holding `seatbelt`, `codex-workspace-write`, `off` or `unavailable`. When `sandbox-exec` is missing or the host is not macOS, the value is `unavailable` and the runner writes one stderr line saying the subject runs unsandboxed. The snapshot check still runs either way.
160: 
161: ---
162: 
163: ## 9. PER-RUNTIME NOTES
164: 
165: | Runtime | Probe status | Recorded behavior |
166: |---------|--------------|-------------------|
167: | Claude Code | probed | Version 2.1.316. The `AskUserQuestion` dialog supports single-select, multi-select and a free-text Other row. The probe records arrow and Enter navigation, `/compact` and resume through the same session ID. |
168: | OpenCode | probed | Version 2.1.4. Session ids must start with `ses_`, so the runner derives one from its UUID and the same `--session` flag resumes it. The `question` dialog toggles a multi-select row with Enter and submits from its Submit tab; the free-text row opens with Enter. The model comes from the root `opencode.json`, which setup must copy. |
169: | Codex | probed | Version 0.164.0. Start-up can show a folder-trust screen, an update offer (always skipped) and a hook review. Hooks stay untrusted unless the script sets `trust_hooks`; then the runner picks "Trust all and continue" and undoes those trust entries after the run. `request_user_input` offers one choice per question, so several choices or an Other answer are typed as a note on its `None of the above` row. Restart uses `codex resume --last` in the scratch folder. Enter must wait 500 ms after typed text, or it lands inside the paste. |
170: | Pi | probed | Version 1.4.0. Two question tools: `question` draws a pick list ending in `Done (...)`, and `ask_user_question` draws a dialog with Space to toggle and a Submit row. The run quits with `/quit`, because `/exit` is sent to the model. `/compact` refuses a session that is still small. |
171: | Devin | probed | Version 3000.11.234. A folder-trust screen opens the first run. The dialog toggles a multi-select row with Space and confirms with Enter; the Other row takes typed text directly. Restart uses `devin --continue` in the scratch folder. Enter must wait 500 ms after typed text. |
172: 
173: Each live MTP-007 run must record the model used by every runtime beside `matrix.md`. If a runtime does not expose its model, record `UNKNOWN` and note what you checked.
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: ## 10. MULTI-RUNTIME LIVE TESTS
178: 
179: Use the script fields below to cover a multi-runtime live test:
180: 
181: | Need | Script form |
182: |------|-------------|
183: | Single-select, multi-select or Other tool question | Use `answer.select` with one or several labels, or `answer.other` for free text. Set `multi: true` when selecting several labels. |
184: | Question asked in plain chat | Use `answer.reply`. |
185: | Process question that must leave no trace | Add an expected question entry, usually `optional: true` when runtimes differ. The turn check asserts that the captured state has no trace. |
186: | Mid-run or final save | Use a `send` turn that requests the save, then a `check` that copies saved files into `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. |
187: | Restart or compaction | Use `action: "restart"` or `action: "compact"`, followed by a state check. |
188: | Kill switch | Put the switch in a separate scenario file's `env` and check that the run wrote nothing. |
189: | Named stages and per-turn state copies | Give each turn an `id` and use its `check` to copy state into `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. |
190: | Runtime results | Pass a comma-separated `--runtime` list. Review each row and evidence path in `matrix.md`. |
191: | Model used | Record each runtime's model next to `matrix.md`. The runner matrix does not have a model column. |
192: 
193: The scenario's `setup` must copy each available runtime project configuration from `$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT` into the scratch project: `.claude/`, `.opencode/`, the root `opencode.json`, `.codex/`, `.pi/` and `.devin/`. Skip a configuration directory when it is missing. The live test then exercises the same project instructions the runtime would read in the repository.
194: 
195: ---

15: # Manual Testing Playbook Prompt Voice - Natural-Human vs RCAF
16: 
17: The full decision for which voice the canonical `Prompt:` field uses in a scenario. `SKILL.md` § Scenario Design Rules carries the summary; this file is the exhaustive detail - the decision table, both sets of voice guidelines, and the default split.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: The canonical `Prompt:` field defaults to **natural-human voice** - how a real user would phrase the request to an AI in conversation. The RCAF (Role-Context-Action-Format) wrapper is the exception, reserved for when the actor IS an AI orchestrator.
24: 
25: **Core Principle**: When in doubt, prefer natural-human. RCAF is the exception, natural is the default.
26: 
27: RCAF wrapper shape:
28: 
29: ```text
30: As a {ROLE}, {ACTION} against {TARGET}. Verify {EXPECTED_OUTCOME}. Return {OUTPUT_FORMAT}.
31: ```
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## 2. DECISION TABLE
36: 
37: | Use **natural-human** when… | Use **RCAF** when… |
38: |---|---|
39: | A human asks the AI directly in conversation ("Review this PR", "Commit my staged changes", "Why is this test flaky?", "Help me start OAuth"). | The actor IS an AI orchestrator delegating to another tool/AI/agent (cross-CLI delegation, multi-agent dispatch, agent handback). |
40: | Code review on a PR, commit/git workflows, bug fixes, code questions, preference questions. | Safety-refusal scenarios where role context determines behavior (e.g., "git safety reviewer" decides whether to refuse a `--no-verify`). |
41: | The scenario could plausibly originate from a Slack DM or a terminal prompt. | Internal validation contracts where the orchestrator IS the operator (e.g., "validation operator validates context retrieval"). |
42: | Default for ~70% of scenarios. | Default for ~30% of scenarios - most often in cli-* and orchestration-heavy playbooks. |
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 3. VOICE GUIDELINES
47: 
48: **Natural-human prompts**:
49: 
50: - Imperative or interrogative ("Review this PR for security issues", "Why is this test flaky?", "Help me start an OAuth feature").
51: - Compact enough for a 9-column table cell (single sentence, ideally ≤25 words).
52: - Specific to the test scenario - not "do a code review" but "Review this auth diff and flag any P0 blockers".
53: - Match the voice of the existing `Real user request:` field, but more compact.
54: 
55: **RCAF prompts when retained**:
56: 
57: - Keep the canonical structure: `As a {ROLE}, {ACTION} against {TARGET}. Verify {EXPECTED_OUTCOME}. Return {OUTPUT_FORMAT}.`
58: - The Role must be an AI orchestrator role (e.g., "external-AI conductor", "git safety reviewer", "validation operator"), NOT a generic human role like "developer" or "engineer".
59: 
60: The `Real user request:` field is always natural-human regardless of which voice the canonical `Prompt:` field uses; it serves as the voice reference baseline.
61: 
62: ---
63:

=== SKILL.md 340-380

- **Single prompt.** The operator sends the Exact Prompt once, reads the answer and judges it against the Expected Signals. The operator collects the evidence by hand.
- **Conversation.** Section 3 carries one `json conversation` block. The shared runner plays each turn into a live runtime session. It answers the runtime's questions, restarts or compacts the session and runs a shell check after every turn. The Exact Prompt is the first turn's `send`, and the Exact Command Sequence is the runner command. The style changes how the scenario runs, not the file's shape.

Apply these questions in order and stop at the first yes:

1. Does the verdict need a person's judgment, such as tone, document quality or whether an explanation is correct? Write a single prompt.
2. Does the behavior need more than one exchange? That means the runtime asks a question back, an answer must change what happens next or state must survive a restart or a compaction. Write a conversation.
3. Must the behavior hold on several runtimes, or does the scenario gate a release as a repeatable regression check? Write a conversation, provided a shell command can decide every turn.
4. Otherwise write a single prompt.

Question 1 comes first because a conversation turn passes only when its check exits 0. When a multi-turn behavior also needs a judged verdict, script the turns a check can decide, and leave the judged part to the operator in the Pass/Fail Criteria, read from that turn's `screen.txt`.

A conversation also needs a runtime the runner drives (`claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex`, `pi` or `devin`), tmux, that runtime installed and logged in and quota to spend. One pass of the runner's own six-turn scenario on all five runtimes took about 11 minutes. The write sandbox needs macOS. Elsewhere the run records `sandbox: unavailable` and the subject runs unsandboxed. When any of these is missing, write a single prompt, or keep the conversation and record `SKIP` with the missing piece as its blocker.

A conversation catches failures that a single exchange never reaches. The runner's own live passes caught a start-up dialog that redrew before it settled (`LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`), a check that failed on one runtime only because of letter case, a spent usage limit (`QUOTA_EXHAUSTED`) and another process writing into the repository during the run (`REPO_CHANGED`). A single prompt costs no runner setup and works with any runtime, so keep it for routing checks, one command's output and anything a reader must judge.

The script is one fenced `json conversation` block under a `### Conversation Script` heading in section 3. See [conversation-scenarios.md](references/conversation-scenarios.md) for the block schema and turn rules. Play a script into a live runtime with the shared runner, from the repository root:

```bash
node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/scripts/run-conversation-scenario.cjs \
  --scenario <scenario.md> --runtime <id[,id...]> --scratch <dir outside the repository> --out <evidence dir>
```

It writes one PASS, FAIL or SKIP row per runtime to `<evidence dir>/matrix.md`, with the evidence for each beside it.

Question 1 comes first because a conversation turn passes only when its check exits 0. When a multi-turn behavior also needs a judged verdict, script the turns a check can decide, and leave the judged part to the operator in the Pass/Fail Criteria, read from that turn's `screen.txt`.

A conversation also needs a runtime the runner drives (`claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex`, `pi` or `devin`), tmux, that runtime installed and logged in and quota to spend. One pass of the runner's own six-turn scenario on all five runtimes took about 11 minutes. The write sandbox needs macOS. Elsewhere the run records `sandbox: unavailable` and the subject runs unsandboxed. When any of these is missing, write a single prompt, or keep the conversation and record `SKIP` with the missing piece as its blocker.

A conversation catches failures that a single exchange never reaches. # Manual Testing Playbook Common Pitfalls

The recurring defects that degrade a manual testing playbook package, why each one breaks the package, and the correct fix. Use this when reviewing a drafted playbook.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Most playbook defects come from splitting package truth across sidecar files, desynchronizing prompt fields, or overloading the root summary with execution detail that belongs in the per-feature file. Each row below pairs the mistake with why it breaks the package and the correct fix.

**Core Principle**: One canonical truth per scenario - shared policy in the root, execution truth in the per-feature file, and nothing duplicated between them.

---

## 2. COMMON PITFALLS

| Mistake | Why It Breaks | Correct Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Keeping separate canonical `review_protocol.md` or `subagent_utilization_ledger.md` files | Splits package truth across sidecar docs | Fold shared review/orchestration rules into the root playbook |
| Using a `snippets/` subtree | No longer matches the current package contract | Put per-feature files in root-level category folders |
| Unsynced prompt fields | Operators do not know which prompt is canonical | Update `SCENARIO CONTRACT`, the table prompt, and the root summary together |
| Broken feature-catalog links | Scenario traceability is lost | Link each scenario to its catalog entry or clearly document the exception |
| Bare command paraphrase prompts | Fails realistic orchestrator-led testing | Rewrite prompts around user intent, evidence, and verdict |
| Overloading root summaries with full execution detail | Root doc becomes noisy and hard to review | Keep full execution truth in the per-feature file |

---

## 3. RELATED RESOURCES

- [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) - § Rules carries the ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE contract these pitfalls map to
- [README.md](README.md) - Reference map for all overflow detail
- [prompt-voice.md](prompt-voice.md) - The natural-human vs RCAF decision behind the prompt-sync fix

15: # Command Creation - Component Choice and Common Pitfalls
16: 
17: The first pitfall is building a command at all when a skill or agent fits better. Pick the component type, then check the draft against the recurring defects below.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: This reference guards two failure modes: the wrong component and the recurring command-authoring defects. A draft that passes this check is the right component, gates its required input, lists only the tools it needs, keeps `description` on one line, and leaves display wording to the presentation asset.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - Before drafting, to confirm the workflow belongs in a command rather than a skill or an agent
30: - After drafting, to review the draft against the mistakes table
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. PICK THE RIGHT COMPONENT FIRST
35: 
36: Choose the component type before drafting.
37: 
38: | Component | Primary Question | Use It When |
39: |---|---|---|
40: | Command | How should a user trigger this workflow? | A slash invocation should gather input and run a repeatable procedure |
41: | Skill | How should this work be done? | Reusable knowledge, standards, templates, or deep guidance are needed |
42: | Agent | Who should do this work? | A named persona needs authority, permissions, and operating rules |
43: 
44: **Practical rule**:
45: - create a command for a user-triggered workflow entry point
46: - create a skill for reusable knowledge or workflow doctrine
47: - create an agent for a durable runtime role with permissions
48: 
49: **Healthy pairing**:
50: - command gathers input and selects mode
51: - skill supplies detailed standards or patterns
52: - agent executes specialized work when delegation is appropriate
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## 3. COMMON MISTAKES
57: 
58: | Mistake | Why It Breaks | Correct Fix |
59: |---|---|---|
60: | Creating a command for reference-only guidance | The slash command becomes a bloated manual instead of an executable workflow | Create or extend a skill/reference instead |
61: | Omitting `argument-hint` for required input | Users cannot see what the invocation expects | Add a precise hint with `<required>` and `[optional]` parts |
62: | Using a required hint without a gate | The command may infer missing input from context | Put the blocking gate after the H1 and its purpose line, before any workflow step |
63: | Treating `:auto` as permission to guess | Autonomous runs can fabricate missing decisions | Fail fast or ask targeted questions when required data is missing |
64: | Putting dashboards in the router | Routing logic becomes hard to audit and presentation cannot evolve independently | Move visible wording to `-presentation.txt` |
65: | Changing behavior while splitting presentation | A refactor becomes a hidden semantic change | Move wording without changing routing, modes, gates, or permissions |
66: | Over-broad `allowed-tools` | The command can use tools outside its contract | Reduce the list to the tools actually required |
67: | Using bare MCP names in `allowed-tools` | Runtime tool resolution can drift from the configured namespace | Use fully qualified `mcp__<server>__<tool>` IDs |
68: | Writing a multi-line description | Help output and metadata consumers expect a single-line summary | Keep `description` one line and move detail into the body |
69: | Adding workflow YAML to every split command | Direct-router command families may not need YAML execution assets | Add `-auto.yaml` and `-confirm.yaml` only when the family routes to workflow assets |
70: | Embedding rationale or meta-commentary in the router body | Design notes, prose-register/framework labels (e.g. "(COSTAR)"), benchmark timings, maintainer sync chores, or "no gap exists" self-attestations are noise a user sees rendered and drift from the truth | Keep the body behavioral. Move rationale to the decision-record/changelog and any render-style rule to the presentation asset |
71: 
72: ---
73:

76: - [README.md](README.md) - command-creation reference map
77: - [argument-hints-and-modes.md](argument-hints-and-modes.md) - correct hint, mode, and frontmatter patterns

79: - [create-agent references](../../sk-create-agent/references/README.md) - sibling packet when the work is really an agent

46: - create a skill for reusable knowledge or workflow doctrine
47: - create an agent for a durable runtime role with permissions
48: 
49: **Healthy pairing**:
50: - command gathers input and selects mode
51: - skill supplies detailed standards or patterns
52: - agent executes specialized work when delegation is appropriate
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## 3. COMMON MISTAKES
57: 
58: | Mistake | Why It Breaks | Correct Fix |
59: |---|---|---|
60: | Creating a command for reference-only guidance | The slash command becomes a bloated manual instead of an executable workflow | Create or extend a skill/reference instead |
61: | Omitting `argument-hint` for required input | Users cannot see what the invocation expects | Add a precise hint with `<required>` and `[optional]` parts |
62: | Using a required hint without a gate | The command may infer missing input from context | Put the blocking gate after the H1 and its purpose line, before any workflow step |
63: | Treating `:auto` as permission to guess | Autonomous runs can fabricate missing decisions | Fail fast or ask targeted questions when required data is missing |
64: | Putting dashboards in the router | Routing logic becomes hard to audit and presentation cannot evolve independently | Move visible wording to `-presentation.txt` |
65: | Changing behavior while splitting presentation | A refactor becomes a hidden semantic change | Move wording without changing routing, modes, gates, or permissions |
66: | Over-broad `allowed-tools` | The command can use tools outside its contract | Reduce the list to the tools actually required |
67: | Using bare MCP names in `allowed-tools` | Runtime tool resolution can drift from the configured namespace | Use fully qualified `mcp__<server>__<tool>` IDs |
68: | Writing a multi-line description | Help output and metadata consumers expect a single-line summary | Keep `description` one line and move detail into the body |
69: | Adding workflow YAML to every split command | Direct-router command families may not need YAML execution assets | Add `-auto.yaml` and `-confirm.yaml` only when the family routes to workflow assets |
70: | Embedding rationale or meta-commentary in the router body | Design notes, prose-register/framework labels (e.g. "(COSTAR)"), benchmark timings, maintainer sync chores, or "no gap exists" self-attestations are noise a user sees rendered and drift from the truth | Keep the body behavioral. Move rationale to the decision-record/changelog and any render-style rule to the presentation asset |
71: 
72: ---

14: # Workflow: baseline, comparison, and lifecycle
15: 
16: Reach for this reference before a document changes, or when both versions are already in hand and the baseline is missing.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: Give every review a real before-state, so a change is judged against what the document actually said.
23: 
24: ### When to Use
25: 
26: - You control the moment before an edit and want the engine to hold the baseline.
27: - No baseline exists, or you are comparing two arbitrary versions.
28: - One review needs to cover multiple files.
29: - You need to inspect or prune stored baselines.
30: 
31: ### Core Principle
32: 
33: The core invariant: **capture the baseline before the edit.** A before/after review needs a real before-state, and once a file is overwritten the original is gone. `create-diff` never mutates the source — capture copies it into a local store.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## 2. AUTOMATIC FLOW (SNAPSHOT-BACKED)
38: 
39: Best when you control the moment before an edit (e.g. an AI is about to modify a document).
40: 
41: ```bash
42: # 1. BEFORE the edit
43: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py snapshot path/to/doc.md
44: 
45: # 2. ... the edit happens ...
46: 
47: # 3. AFTER the edit
48: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py compare path/to/doc.md --report review.html
49: ```
50: 
51: `compare` uses the file's **latest** snapshot as the "before" and the current file as the "after". If no snapshot exists it exits `4` and tells you to snapshot first or use the explicit pair.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## 3. EXPLICIT-PAIR FLOW (FALLBACK)
56: 
57: Best when there is no baseline, when comparing two arbitrary versions, or when the automatic store is unavailable or unwanted.
58: 
59: ```bash
60: python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py compare-pair \
61:   --before old.md --after new.md \
62:   --label-before "v1" --label-after "v2" \
63:   --report review.html
64: ```
65: 
66: No stored state is read or written. `--label-before`/`--label-after` set the names shown in the report (default: the file names).
67:

 ## 1. OVERVIEW
 
+### Purpose
+

+

+### Core Principle
+
 The core invariant: **capture the baseline before the edit.** A before/after review needs a real before-state, and once a file is overwritten the original is gone. `create-diff` never mutates the source — capture copies it into a local store.

Writes are atomic (temp file + rename); the source is only ever read.

21	## 1. OVERVIEW
    22	
    23	Write a conversation scenario when the behavior depends on multiple prompts, scripted answers, runtime actions, or state checks across a session. One prompt is enough when a single request and its result capture the full behavior. The ordered decision rule, the runtime requirements and the cost of each style live in `SKILL.md` §6, Choosing the Scenario Style.
    24	
    25	The script is one fenced `json conversation` block in section 3 of the scenario file. The block is the source of truth for the conversation turns.
   120	- Start the scenario file from `assets/manual-testing-playbook-conversation-snippet-template.md`.
   121	- Put one `json conversation` block in each scenario file under `### Conversation Script` in section 3.
   122	- The first `send` must equal the scenario contract prompt.
   123	- A second scratch project or a different `env` is a separate scenario file and runner invocation.
   124	- Compaction followed by a send is two turns: one turn with `action: compact` and its check, then a turn with the send.
   125	- A turn with neither `send` nor `action` is check-only. The first turn holding one of those fields must be a `send`.
   126	- The validator checks the block but never runs `setup` or `check` commands.
   127	- Never match a model reply with `grep -x` or `grep -Fx` on `screen.txt`. Runtime prefixes prevent an exact line match: Claude replies start with `⏺ `, Codex with `• `, Pi with ` ● `, Devin with a leading space and OpenCode with five spaces. Use `grep -F` with a distinctive marker.
   128	- `screen.txt` shows a visible 50-row pane that retains earlier turns and the current turn's echoed send. Inspect only text after that turn's echoed send by using the `awk` pattern in [the session resume example](../../../../skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-claude-code/manual-testing-playbook/session-continuity/resume-specific-session-by-id-conversation.md), or check a marker the model can learn only by reading a file. Never put the expected marker in a `send`.
   129	- A check can read the turn's evidence from `$CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR`. The raw pane slice in `raw-pane.log` and the full plain-text scrollback in `history.txt` both exist before the check runs. `history.txt` is the right file to search for text that a long reply may have scrolled off the 50-row `screen.txt`. `raw-pane.log` carries terminal escape codes between words, so a plain `grep` on it is unreliable.
   130	- The scratch project inherits the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so before any file write the model asks the spec-folder question in plain chat. For every turn that writes, add a `questions` entry with `"answer": {"reply": "D"}` and `"optional": true`. An `other` answer belongs only in a runtime question dialog, never in plain chat. Use `reply` for chat questions.
   131	- The scratch starts without skills. When a scenario needs a skill, setup must copy the repository skills and the runtime project configuration into scratch with `cp -R "$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT/.skilled" .skilled` and `cp -R "$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT/.claude" .claude`, replacing `.claude` with `.opencode`, `.pi` or `.devin` when that runtime requires it. Their relative symlinks resolve after `.skilled` is copied. Never symlink into the repository because the runner refuses the run with `CONTAINMENT_ESCAPED`.
   132	- Do not coach the behavior under test. Each `send` must be the plain user request. Do not tell the model to ask a question, pause, refuse or name which tool it used.
   133	- A question's `match` regular expression must identify the question asked and must not match any text in the echoed `send`.
   134	- If a required precondition is missing, such as a fixture, credential, tool or network access, setup must exit with status `77` and print a one-line reason to skip the runtime. Its first non-empty output line is the blocker. A check can exit `77` to skip its turn.
   135	- Checks must only read state. Nothing may write under `$CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT`.
   136	
   151	Each runtime folder contains `result.json`, `actions.jsonl`, `raw-pane.log`, `setup.log`, `repo-before.txt`, `repo-after.txt` and `checkpoints.tsv`. Each turn folder contains `screen.txt`, `history.txt`, its `raw-pane.log` slice, one `question-N.txt` file per detected question and `check.txt`. The evidence root contains `matrix.md`, with one verdict and evidence path per requested runtime.
   152	
   153	The runner sets `CONVERSATION_RUNTIME`, `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT`, `CONVERSATION_RUN_DIR` (the runtime's evidence folder) and `CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR` (the turn's evidence folder) for each `check` command. A check defaults to 60 seconds. Set `CONVERSATION_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` to override that bound. An overrun fails as `CHECK_TIMEOUT`. Each `setup` command has 120 seconds. An overrun refuses the run as `SETUP_TIMEOUT`. Exit 77 skips the runtime with its first non-empty output line as the blocker. The runner sets `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT` and `CONVERSATION_RUNTIME` for every `setup` command too, so setup can copy project files from the repository without any variable set by hand. `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT` is the repository the run snapshots, which `--repo-root` can point at a worktree.
